name: Joseph Kabila
role: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (2001–2019); FRN leader (since October 2026)
summary: Kabila combined private investment and infrastructure development with stronger national participation in mining. His democratic pledges coexist with an extensively documented record of repression and delayed elections; in October 2026 he assumed leadership of an armed opposition coalition.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He promotes liberalization and private competition as engines of development.

public-ownership.rationale: He expands compulsory state shareholding in mining, alongside continued private investment.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He signed stronger mining requirements despite industry lobbying.

empower-police-military.rationale: He calls for a powerful, professional and better-equipped national army.

decide-locally.rationale: He endorses constitutional decentralization into 26 provinces.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He signed the Paris Agreement and explicitly called compliance crucial.

revolution-justified.rationale: His new FRN expressly seeks the incumbent’s removal, including through armed force.

central-planning.rationale: He favors liberalized investment rather than government allocation throughout the economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His industrial program channels infrastructure and resource finance toward strategic development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He proposes broader access to land titles, housing ownership and credit for ordinary citizens.

democracy-best.rationale: Spoke of democracy while delaying the presidential election due in 2016 by two years beyond his mandate; mixed.

right-to-secede.rationale: He insists on maintaining national unity and territorial integrity.

political-violence-never.rationale: He leads a political-military coalition expressly willing to use force against the incumbent.

direct-action.rationale: His armed coalition pursues removal by force, while he also insists on political dialogue and democracy.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His program explicitly accelerates petroleum, coal and oil-shale exploitation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Invoked the people's choice while staying in office two years past his term without an election; mixed.

party-controls-media.rationale: His government closed critical media, whereas his latest program promises fundamental freedoms.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: His parity law imposes penalties on artistic and audiovisual representations violating dignity and established morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He defended the consecutive-term restriction, while prolonged holdover complicates his constitutional claims.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He signed a law defining parity as equal representation in decision-making bodies.

patriotic-education.rationale: He proposes civic education emphasizing national loyalty and sacrifice for the homeland.

delink-world-market.rationale: He explicitly seeks private foreign investment and international economic integration.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He urges collective action against what he describes as dictatorship and constitutional breakdown.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He prioritizes domestic resources for industrial finance to avoid excessive foreign borrowing.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His government repressed opponents; his latest speech demands fundamental liberties and inclusive dialogue.

term-limits.rationale: He defended the two-term constitution and eventually left, after extending his second term through delayed elections.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 2016 reform introduces mutual agreement for legal acts but retains the husband as household head.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He demands armed groups’ neutralization but now leads a coalition incorporating rebel military structures.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: His signed law requires eliminating practices obstructing women’s ownership and control of property.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: His government cut internet and messaging services to disrupt political protests.

women-suffrage.rationale: His parity law explicitly grants women and men equal political rights and electoral participation.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: His law establishes an interministerial committee and national gender and parity council.

national-resource-control.rationale: His mining law increases mandatory state equity and Congolese participation.

notes: No inferred answers. Reviewed all 490 statements and remaining nulls by theme. Neither a party label nor the in-absentia 2025 conviction is used to infer personal positions. The October 2026 FRN leadership is independently documented and supersedes the categorical rejection of political violence in his 2016 speech. Public ownership is limited support for mining equity, not a claim that he favors comprehensive nationalization. Liberalization and resource regulation are distinct documented policies. Inclusion failure, if any, is retained.
